items.title: Modder Deliberately Corrupts Their Own Hugely Popular Total War: Warhammer III Mod as Row Over AI Escalates
items.description: The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.

Veteran modder Venris has created Simply Fun Overhaul (SFO) mods for Total War: Warhammer for years, with a popular Patreon helping in the development of the latest version, SFO: Grimhammer III. The mod overhauls the base game to be closer to the lore and Warhammer universe, changing everything from the campaign and battle mechanics to the economy and customization.

Recently, people have used AI to release sub mods of SFO: Grimhammer III that work with updated versions of the main, Creative Assembly-developed video game, without asking permission. In response, Venris corrupted their own mod so that it stops working with these uploads, and threatened to make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“Due to the growing number of unauthorized reuploads of SFO: Grimhammer III, and more importantly, the use of AI in the process, I have deliberately corrupted the mod to prevent it from functioning with such unauthorized uploads,” Venris said in a statement published online. “If this situation continues to escalate, I will make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“SFO: Grimhammer is the result of nearly 10 years of passion and love for this community and the fantasy world. As such, I do not permit anyone to take my work without permission. Especially not for AI-related purposes.

“Support modders, not AI.”

Recent weeks have seen an explosion of AI-generated “mods,” which have called into question not just mod creation, but the very foundations of the video game industry. Clips of gameplay showing AI-generated “game-merging mods” have gone viral on social media, with others releasing AI-generated versions of games running on platforms they have yet to be officially released on. Some have used AI to add or expand features, increase player counts, or fuse parts of two different games together.

The mods have raised eyebrows online, and sparked questions about the legality of their release. Some within the traditional modding community have expressed shock and disappointment in AI-generated clones and mashups, and have questioned the continued viability of their hobby.

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Fallout video game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda, leading fans to celebrate.

But not all oppose AI-generated mods, clones, or video games. “Oh no the horror,” one person said in response to Venris’ post. “Someone forget to get a rubberstamp from a bureaucrat modder whose work depends on the original game devs and publishers anyway. You guys are such losers.”

Most, though, have backed Venris on this. “Anyone that thinks that you are doing something bad here doesn't have experience with someone stealing something that they have spent a major chunk of their life making and it shows,” one person said.

items.title: Disney President Reacts to Live-Action Moana Flop, Says It Was an 'Excellent Film' Hit by 'Unusual Circumstances'
items.description: Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."

Speaking this week at the Bloomberg Screentime event (via Variety), Walden framed Moana's poor performance as a result of the movie industry being competitive, and the film simply launching at the wrong time.

"It's so competitive right now that you have to have... the right film at the right time, with audiences feeling a certain degree of demand," Walden stated. "I would say our live-action Moana, which is excellent, I think it was hurt by the proximity to our second animated version of Moana, which came together under unusual circumstances, but premiered about 18 months before this one."

The unusual circumstances Walden is referring to here relate to Disney's relatively last-minute pivot that saw Moana 2 change from launching as a Disney+ series to a theatrical movie. This resulted in the project being slotted into Disney's film schedule awkwardly just a year and a half before the long-gestating plans for a live-action film.

"Perhaps there was not enough time to create a lot of pent-up demand for another film," Walden concluded.

While most would agree the timing was indeed awkward, it's fair to point out that this issue is one entirely of Disney's own making. (Perhaps the live-action movie would have performed better if it was held back until a year later, with Moana 2 more of a distant meory?)

But then there's also the matter of the movie's quality. While Walden is unlikely to say anything other than the film being great, the majority of critics disagreed. Moana sits with a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with an average rating of 4.8/10. Pre-release, the film's trailers were also subject to audience criticism over the movie's CGI backgrounds and a slew of memes over Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson's luscious wig.

"Dwayne Johnson returns as Maui opposite newcomer Catherine Laga'aia in this frame-by-frame retelling of the Disney animated musical that doesn't do enough to justify being made," IGN wrote in our live-action Moana review, awarding the movie a 6/10.

While the Moana franchise will continue with a third animated film following the breakout success of Moana 2, there's no word of a live-action sequel being made. You're welcome, indeed.

items.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Filming Delay Reports Spark Concern That Marvel's Multiverse Saga Finale May Be Postponed
items.description: Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.

This week, an array of Marvel movie insiders reported hearing that filming on Marvel's big Multiverse Saga finale will now begin later than planned, after previously being set to start last month.

Serial MCU tipsters Daniel Richtman, Alex Perez, and Apocalyptic Horseman appear to have independently verified that Secret Wars shooting will now take place early in 2027, likely in January, sparking concern among fans about the impact this hold up will potentially have.

It's worth making clear that Marvel is yet to give any official update on its production schedule, and it ultimately may not need to do so if there's no impact on Secret Wars' planned December 17, 2027 launch date. That said, the potential of the movie's shooting schedule changing has many fans questioning if the film can still be completed in time.

"Gives the cast time to promote Doomsday during this winter," Marvel fan BTSMGL wrote in one of several lengthy threads on reddit. "I'm not in a rush for Ghost Rider so as long as we get X-Men and BP3 still in 2028, I'm fine with this."

"A *lot* is riding on Doomsday," added vadermaulkylo. "They’re probably waiting to see how it's received before committing to anything. If Doomsday gets a bad critical and/or audience reception then that'll drastically change what they'd do in its second act film."

"I'm getting tired of waiting," concluded own-papaya-4264. "Secret Wars was announced in 2022 for Christs sake."

Principal photography for Avengers: Doomsday lasted five months from April to September 2025, with additional material believed to have been recently shot ahead of the film's December launch. In other words, Marvel has had just over a year to work with the bulk of its footage in post-production.

Just for comparison, Spider-Man: Brand New Day was filmed between August and December 2025, for launch in July 2026. This is a much tighter turnaround of the kind fans now think Secret Wars will need, though Brand New Day is arguably a more straightforward project when compared to Avengers' enormous story scope and sprawling cast list.

Much remains unknown, including the exact date Secret Wars will now begin shooting, and whether Marvel has already banked footage it will incorporate into the movie while previously shooting Doomsday — a tactic used for Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame. Could Secret Wars get delayed? It's possible, though any sense that the film's launch could slip into 2028 would then likely impact the release of Marvel's three subsequent projects already scheduled for that year (X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3).

Still, if a delay is needed to ensure Secret Wars lands as Marvel hopes, a longer wait doesn't seem out of the question. Last month, directors Joe and Anthony Russo teased that Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, which has a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.

items.title: Person Behind Viral AI-Generated Fallout: New York Game Hauls It Offline, Says Bethesda Issued Cease and Desist
items.description: The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.

Earlier this week, a self-styled “AI creative” known as “CHRIS FIRST” on X / Twitter published a video of Fallout: New York, a game built by Claude Opus 5.5 and made playable in a browser. It included quests, companions, dialogue trees, Fallout’s iconic V.A.T.S. combat and even a working Pip-Boy.

Fallout: New York, a full Fallout game you play in your browser, built with Claude Opus 5.5.

Quests. Dialogue trees. V.A.T.S. A working Pip-Boy.

Zero texture files. Zero sound files. Every building, weapon, face and sound is generated by code. pic.twitter.com/58Vls0mOYx

— CHRIS FIRST (@chrisfirst) September 28, 2026

The initial video, viewed 3.5 million times on X / Twitter, sparked a debate about the rights and wrongs of CHRIS FIRST’s use of AI, with some calling the game AI slop, and others impressed by the gameplay. As you’d expect, many responded to the video to predict that Bethesda would eventually step in, although CHRIS FIRST seemed somewhat naive to the situation.

“It’s all free and I make 0 money on it,” he tweeted. “I hope they don’t ask me to take it down. I really love Fallout and this was just a fun tech demo. But I should add a quest where you have to serve someone papers, but they keep running away.”

The inevitable now appears to have happened. CHRIS FIRST published an image of what looks like an official cease and desist from Bethesda parent company, ZeniMax Media Inc, which points to trademark infringement for the use of the 'fallout.nyc' domain name, as well as its use of copyrighted material. IGN has asked Microsoft for comment.

CHRIS FIRST, meanwhile, remained defiant in his post even as he confirmed the removal of the game. “Hey, @BethesdaStudios,” they said, “how about you make a Fallout game instead so I don’t have to? Sorry to everyone who enjoyed the game! But the suits got involved and the fun is over.”

No-one is particularly surprised by Bethesda’s action here. “Dude this game was ass and didn’t even look like Fallout,” one person said. “I don’t know why you tried to cash in on their IP lmao. They had every right to C and D you.”

“How about you make some original game instead of copying existing one?” another person suggested. “Like no one saw this coming from a mile away. Ppl can't expect to rip off an IP and not get dmca'd,” another said. One person commented: “Everything ur AI game did was already done before In Fallout just mixed around. No new mechanics or innovation.”

“Wow it’s almost like stealing is bad,” another said. “Not sure what you expected with your AI trash,” one person declared. "I would genuinely rather play Fallout Tactics than this AI generated garbage," another said. "Everyone liked that," Karl Schecht, aka professional 3D and technical artist and YouTuber Kommander Karl, said.

This week has seen a number of viral clips of AI-generated “game-merging mods” in which Minecraft is fused with other famous games in what is a growing and controversial trend. One such video, which shows Minecraft copied into Elden Ring, was viewed 22 million times on X / Twitter.

I put the entire of game minecraft into elden ring as mod. its runs on Mac. pic.twitter.com/CojefjxtLn

— Anime Girl Worshiper (@TobynJacobs) September 29, 2026

This in turn has sparked a significant debate about the legality around AI-generated clones and these “game-merging mods,” with some wondering if publishers will step in to take action or push for guardrails that prevent their creation within the AI models themselves. One person has released an AI-generated Splatoon clone, which some believe Nintendo will take a look at sooner rather than later. Another person merged Mario with Elden Ring.

so long, gay margit https://t.co/W96dFvpjYI pic.twitter.com/pTTodFIq9v

— Deltaroo Δ (@Deltaroo3D) September 30, 2026

As the debate over AI-generated games rages on, video game publishers will be desperate to keep a tight leash on their franchises. AI is making what was traditionally a painstaking process of reverse-engineering and recompilation significantly faster, which has prompted some to wonder about the future of commercial video game development. Why buy a Switch 2 if you can have AI generate a clone of one of Nintendo's exclusives? Others, though, have pointed out that none of these game-merging mods or clones display any creativity or present any new ideas, rather take existing popular video games and either mash them together or simply replicate what is already playable better elsewhere.

Bethesda is of course working on a number of official Fallout games, including Fallout 5, Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters, and a spinoff from Fallout: New Vegas developer Obsidian Entertainment. None has a release window, although new Xbox boss Asha Sharma has talked about wanting to double down on the company's biggest franchises, including Fallout.

items.title: Justin Wong and IFC Yipes Literally Commentate Ryu's Match Against Blanka in the Street Fighter Movie
items.description: We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.

Director Kitao Sakurai made sure the fighting game community felt represented in his Street Fighter film, inviting Justin Wong, IFC Yipes, and Maximilian Dood to play criminals in an apparent Shadaloo prison while Blanka (Jason Momoa) and Ryu (Andrew Koji) duke it out for M. Bison’s viewing pleasure.

These three community pillars were shown in a short teaser for the movie back in July. Come October 1, Wong shared some behind-the-scenes footage of his time on set, which included a closer look at the scene he shared with Yipes.

Previously, we only saw the two fighting game pros-turned-commentators going bananas for Blanka and Ryu’s brawl; Wong’s footage shows himself and Yipes literally commentating the match, betting on commissary rations like ramen noodles and toilet paper.

It’s fantastic stuff, and it isn’t the only homage to the competitive scene that's included in the movie. Working with the makeup artists, Wong also gave his character a tattoo of the number 37 — and you can probably guess why he chose that particular ink. (He joked that his character had gotten sent to prison for stabbing someone who kept parrying him, saying, ‘You can’t parry a knife.’)

Speaking of Moment 37, Wong even got recognized by Noah Centineo (Ken), who asked which of the group was responsible for parrying Ken in “that sick-ass fight.” (Wong sheepishly admitted that he was the one who got parried, and later taught Centineo some moves in the game.)

All of the guest influencers got a tour of a few of the film’s sets, which included a look at some of the movie’s props. One of those props appeared to be Mike Haggar’s pipe, which would be an insane reference to include but not totally unexpected, given that Final Fight and Street Fighter take place in the same universe.

Street Fighter hurricane kicks its way into theaters on October 16, 2026. In the meantime, you can check out our interview with David Dastmalchian (M. Bison), who told us all about how he studied real-life dictators to bring Shadaloo’s leader to life.

items.description: Doom: The Dark Ages developer id Software has announced a new free update coming to the first-person shooter's Revelations DLC next month: an endless single-player "Slaughter Mode."
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Doom: The Dark Ages developer id Software has announced a new free update coming to the first-person shooter's Revelations DLC next month: an endless single-player "Slaughter Mode."

items.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
items.description: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.

As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show. The series is slated to premier in 2028, the same year that the very last movie in the franchise is also set to release.

Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever, is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise.

Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles.

“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.”

Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead.

Image Credits: Earl Gibson III/Deadline via Getty Images

items.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
items.description: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.

If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God.

The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.”

I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice.

As shared by The Hollywood Reporter, the film has been greenlit by Lionsgate Studios, with Sam Raimi for Ghost House Pictures and Jordan Peele for Monkeypaw set to produce. This is the first time these two have collaborated on a project together.

They aren’t the first to get their hands on Clark’s IP, though; Portrait of God was previously snagged by Universal, but the project fell through in early 2026. Things seem substantially more stable now, given the producers attached, as well as a major actress set to star in the film: Chase Infiniti, who gained wide acclaim for her breakout role in One Battle After Another.

“We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with Dylan Clark, whose remarkable talent and distinctive perspective make him one of the most exciting emerging voices in horror,” Lionsgate film’s Adam Fogelson said in a statement. “With Sam and Jordan, two of the genre’s most influential producers, the extraordinary Chase Infiniti starring, and Dylan at the helm, this is an exceptional creative team. We believe they have all the ingredients for a film that is haunting, thought-provoking, and scary as hell.”

“With Blair Witch, I’m experiencing firsthand the trust Lionsgate places in its filmmakers, and I couldn’t be happier that Portrait of God has found a home there, as well,” Clark added. “I’m also thrilled to welcome Chase Infiniti to our team. She blew me away in One Battle After Another and is one of the most exciting young actors working today.”

It’s a big time for indie horror flicks, especially where YouTubers are concerned; Kane Parsons’ Backrooms and Curry Barker’s Obsession were smash hits at the box office, opening the way for adaptations of other popular internet creepypastas like Siren Head (to be produced by Zach Cregger), The Mandela Catalogue, and even The SCP Foundation.

Image Credits: Monica Schipper/Getty Images

items.title: Lanterns Rakes In More Than 18 Million Views Per Episode Globally As Season Finale Approaches
items.description: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.

As shared by Variety, statistics compiled by media research firm Nielsen show that Lanterns’ seventh episode accrued seven million views within the United States during its first three days, combined across HBO’s cable channels and its streaming service, HBO Max.

In the US, Lanterns is reportedly averaging more than 12 million views per episode; that number increases to 19 million when taking global viewership into account. Variety notes that it’s highly likely these numbers will continue to rise, as 1.5 million new viewers reportedly watched Lanterns’ premier episode just last week.

This is good news for fans of the newly-rebooted DCU, but it’s not surprising; Lanterns has been a big hit with audiences and critics alike, though it’s caused no end of debate among hardcore Lanterns fans, given the fate of one of its central characters. (There’s still hope that this particular person might still be around, though, thanks to some convincing theories making the rounds online.)

With these latest stats in mind, Lanterns is rubbing elbows with other uber-popular HBO releases; DC’s previous series on the streamer, The Penguin, averaged 27 million views per episode back in 2024, while shows like Euphoria averaged 25 million per episode by the end of its third and final season. Award-winning medical drama The Pitt averaged 15.4 million views on Season 2, the finale of which garnered 9.7 million views.

Lanterns is gearing up for its season finale, which airs on HBO Max this coming Sunday, October 4. We have a few burning questions that still need to be answered, and its latest episode has fueled oodles of fan theories, not to mention memes (mostly about Mogo and John Stewart).

IGN’s Jesse Schedeen scored its latest episode an eight out of 10, praising it for regaining the series lost momentum from episode seven and reconnecting with the “core Hal/John dynamic we love so much."

items.title: New GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms Game Will Feature Sex Scenes
items.description: GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.

In New Zealand and Australia, GTA 6's store page on PlayStation was updated to include the game's official age rating. A similar thing happened this morning with the UK and American versions of the game, but the New Zealand and Australia versions offer one distinct difference: the mention of sex scenes. Yes, it's true: there will be intercourse in GTA 6.

If you're asking yourself, "Is that different from GTA 5?" Currently, it's a bit unclear. GTA 5's brief rating description on the store page makes no mention of sex scenes, despite there being at least one. Midway through the game, Trevor can be seen getting freaky with Johnny Klebitz's girlfriend (granted, it's pretty brief). Instead, the ratings description just mentions "Sex."

It's unclear if the ratings boards have evolved their language since GTA 5's release nearly a decade and a half ago, or if GTA 6 will feature more scripted, detailed sex scenes more comparable to a film or TV show. It's also possible that the more general, less specific description for GTA 5 is more pointedly referencing the ability to pick up sex workers and engage in intercourse with them. Ratings boards may view these gameplay moments differently from heavily mo-capped sex scenes featured in cutscenes.

GTA 6's sex scenes may be much more focused and graphic, especially since the story revolves around the romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia. Various trailers have shown sensual, intimate scenes between the two characters, so it's possible that the full game will feature some pretty spicy material. Ultimately, all we can do is speculate until we get detailed breakdowns of the specific content that led to this rating, which will surely follow in the coming weeks.

Ultimately, it looks like Rockstar isn't pulling any punches with GTA 6. Rating descriptions have mentioned blood and gore, intense violence, drug use, and more, so it looks like we're in for yet another edgy GTA game. The developer has managed to keep a lot under wraps, but recently revealed that it visited strip clubs in Florida for "research purposes."

We're officially just a month away from GTA 6's release date, so there are sure to be many more marketing beats in the coming weeks. Whether that brings a new trailer or other forms of marketing remains to be seen, but Rockstar has shelled out serious dough for an ad on top of the Miami Heat's arena in Florida and has begun placing ads in New York as of today.

Editor's note: Added clarity and context around GTA 5's original rating and sexual content.

items.title: Miami Vice '85 Casts Walton Goggins in Villain Role
items.description: Walton Goggins has joined the cast of Miami Vice '85. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character, who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Walton Goggins will play a villain in Miami Vice '85.

Deadline reports that Goggins, who has made a name for himself in recent years via Fallout and The White Lotus, will leverage his nefarious qualities on the big screen in 2028. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character, who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film.

The two villains will be contending with characters played by Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler, who will play Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.

Not much is known about the film right now, but it is expected to be a period reboot of the iconic TV series. It's not a sequel to Michael Mann's own film adaptation of the TV series or an extension of the original source material.

The film will be helmed by F1 and Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski. The project was initially slated for a 2027 release, but was pushed back to May 2028. It is expected to begin filming sometime this year, so expect more casting announcements in the coming weeks as production ramps up.

Walton Goggins has made a name for himself by playing treacherous characters. He made the rounds as a variety of shady TV characters on shows like Justified, The Shield, and more. He has also starred in films like The Hateful Eight, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and Tomb Raider. He's arguably best known these days for playing The Ghoul, a sort of anti-hero in Fallout that has been corrupted by the Wasteland while searching for his long-lost family.

Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for W Magazine

items.title: Amazon Launches New Line of Kindles and Accessories Right Before Prime Big Deal Days
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Amazon has revealed its 2026 line of Kindle devices just a few days before its Prime Big Deal Days sale. The refresh includes a brand new Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite, and Kindle Colorsoft, along with new accessories and Kids Editions of these tablets.

All of the new devices and accessories are now available to buy or preorder on Amazon, and you can check out the official press release for specifics on each device. With the release of new models, older Kindle devices are getting discounted as part of Amazon's sale as well.

New Kindle Device Pricing and Details

Amazon releases new Kindle devices pretty much every year, and in the past, the improvements were incremental. The biggest changes to the 2026 models include Amazon making them thinner, lighter, and faster than previous iterations of the e-readers. It also introduced aluminum hardware options and other highly requested features like cover page turning for their new Signature Editions of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft models.

According to Amazon's press release, the new standard Kindle will be 30% faster when opening books and will have edge-to-edge color across the full lineup.

The Kindle is still arguably the best reading tablet on the market. With Amazon removing support for older device models earlier this year, it's worth considering an upgrade to a newer version.

It's important to note that all Kindle devices released after 2024 will include most of the latest features and will be compatible with newer accessories via Bluetooth.

The Kindle Click Is the Best New Accessory

A Kindle is already pretty convenient, but what if it could be even more convenient? Amazon has announced a remote that will turn the pages for you. Third-party Kindle page-turners have been available for years now, but this is the first time Amazon has made a Bluetooth-compatible version that doesn't actually need to physically touch the screen to get the page to turn. At $34.99, the new Amazon Kindle Click will work with any Kindle model released in 2024 or later. It's currently set to release on October 28 alongside most of the new 2026 Kindles.

In addition to the remote, Amazon is also releasing new Kindle covers that include physical page-turning buttons. Both of these new accessories are bringing back a physical experience to an otherwise digital product.

items.title: Danny McBride's G.I. Joe Movie Casts Bradley Cooper as Duke
items.description: Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride.

McBride has been developing a new G.I. Joe movie for Paramount for some time, and it appears to be gaining some steam. After months of rumors, Deadline reports that Bradley Cooper will star as Duke, the leader of the titular group. McBride has reportedly had Cooper at the top of his wishlist for the film's cast, but there were questions over whether or not it was feasible. Cooper is currently starring in and directing an Ocean's 11 prequel in Europe, so he's got his hands full. However, Deadline claims that Cooper liked the script so much that he signed on and committed to the film.

As of right now, it's unclear when the film will shoot, but presumably it won't be sometime until next summer at the earliest. items.title: New Pokémon x ESA Collection Includes the Astronaut Pikachu Plush That Went to Space
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Pokémon's collaboration with the European Space Agency has officially led to a merch drop. The new collection includes two new Pikachu plushies, listed at $29.99, which feature the electric-type Pokemon in two versions of the ESA space suit.

Recognize the design? The new plush is modelled after the Pikachu plush ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot took on her flight to the International Space Station earlier this year. The collection also includes apparel, pins, and plenty of TCG accessories, now available directly from The Pokémon Center.

Pokemon x ESA Collection Drops Ahead of World Space Week

The collaboration between Pokémon and ESA kicked off on April 11, when the original astronaut Pikachu plush was launched into space. The plush spent a grand total of 67 days in orbit at the International Space Station, circling Earth over 1,000 times.

Now, the partnership is coming back to Earth. The Pokémon Center's new collection is dropping ahead of World Space Week, which kicks off on October 4. That date will also see the launch of a new space-themed event in Pokémon GO and interactive “Space and Pokémon” exhibitions in select museums across Europe.

For those of us on the other side of the pond? Well, at least we get merch. The new TCG accessories, led by a binder, deck box, and playmat, all show illustrations of astronaut Pikachu floating alongside Lunatone, Cosmog, and Minior.

Fans can also get their hands on T-shirts and hoodies with the same cosmic Pokémon graphic. The most expensive item in the drop is a full bomber jacket, listed at $129.99, which features individual Pokémon patches and a Poké Ball zipper.

The Pokémon franchise is marking its 30th anniversary this year, and there have been plenty of partnerships to celebrate. Here’s TPC’s statement on the ethos behind this particular collaboration:

“The European Space Agency (ESA) is Europe’s gateway to space. Its mission is to shape the development of Europe’s space capability and ensure that investment in space continues to deliver benefits to the citizens of Europe and the world. Together, ESA and Pokémon aim to inspire and delight with endless cosmic possibility!”

While most of the collection is available for purchase now, one "delightful and inspiring" item that still doesn't have a release date is a new figure of Pikachu in his astronaut outfit. Just another thing for fans to look forward to during the long wait for Gen 10.

items.title: Riot Games Co-Founder Says 2XKO Needed ‘Hundreds of Thousands, if Not Millions’ of Monthly Active Players to Survive
items.description: The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community.

Speaking on The Lemonade Stand, Merrill went into detail about what happened behind the scenes at Riot to cause 2XKO’s catastrophic failure, and provided a ballpark figure of monthly active users the game would have needed in order to justify how much money and time was spent on its development.

It’s no surprise that this figure was, to put it lightly, pretty unrealistic for a fighting game; Merrill said that, considering its cost structure, 2XKO would have needed a player count “in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions” to rationalize its continued support.

Merrill also mentioned Street Fighter 6, saying the 2023 release of Capcom’s juggernaut title threw off their plans to take a big chunk of the fighting game community’s interest off the back of Street Fighter V.

“I think we had a window to do some great things to really help the fighting game community, and then Street Fighter 6 came out, which was something like eight years after we started working on 2XKO,” Merrill explained. “We had an awesome development team of really talented people that did great work, that made a beautiful game. We’d already communicated all this stuff to players, and so we were like, ‘You know what? Let’s just keep going. Let’s give it to the community. Let’s see what happens, right?’ …I think if we came out, ideally when we should’ve, years before Street Fighter, I think we would have made a really significant impact on the community.”

Merrill explained that Riot didn’t have internal “alignment” on the strategy for 2XKO, which caused “managerial fracturing” and confusion within the team. Ultimately, not enough players hopped on the game in order to justify the time and money spent on it, so Riot did what they thought was best — issued full refunds to players and canceled further content updates.

“We’ve got nobody to blame but ourselves,” he said. “[2XKO] resonated with some players, but not nearly enough players in order to justify the sort of live service, long-tail approach that the game was designed to do. And so we were like, let’s just pivot, let’s create this box, give everybody a refund, say, ‘Hey, sorry we weren't able to achieve this incredibly high aspiration that we were trying to do for the fighting game community, but we love you guys, appreciate [you], hope they’ll play this game, like many other box games, for years to come, and here you go. Sorry we let you down,’ is sort of the orientation of what happened there.”

For comparison, Street Fighter 6 — which is indisputably the biggest fighting game on the market right now — boasts an average of anywhere between 16,000 and 20,000 monthly active users on Steam (not including PlayStation, which doesn't share these statistics publicly). It’s understandable that Riot, the maker of massively popular MOBA League of Legends, might expect more than that — but even Riot themselves knew there was no way they could reach “millions” of monthly active users to justify keeping their tag fighter alive.

Unsurprisingly, Merrill’s comments have sparked a swath of heated reactions within the fighting game community. Most players were left stunned that Riot felt such a high player count was necessary to keep 2XKO afloat, given how relatively "niche" the genre is.

“It seems like they figured the game wasn't going to last long, but they spent so much money on it, so instead of immediately canning it, they released it to see if it would do anything,” one player mused. “Unfortunately, what it needed to do goes way beyond what any fighting game has ever done in existence lol.”

“The way [Merrill said], ‘Then Street Fighter 6 came out,’ like that wasn't going to happen. SFV had one of the best comeback stories in fighting games. Did he really not think 6 was going to happen?” another asked.

2XKO was first revealed to the public as ‘Project L’ in 2019, though rumors of a fighting game based on the League of Legends IP had been swirling around long beforehand. Its confusing release (from a closed beta to extended early access) on the back of a lengthy development period essentially killed most of the hype around the game, and Riot officially announced plans to end active development after December 2026, though online play will still be supported.

items.title: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023 in Pictures
items.description: GTA 6 officially releases next month, so we're taking a look at how the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, have evolved since their 2023 reveal.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 officially releases next month, so we're taking a look at how the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, have evolved since their 2023 reveal.

If there's one thing Rockstar has consistently managed to achieve, it's that its finished games often look better than the reveal trailers. That isn't the case for many game studios. In fact, a lot of games have been slammed for being downgraded between their reveals and launches. Watch Dogs, Cyberpunk 2077, and BioShock Infinite are all solid games, but they looked even better when they were initially revealed.

GTA 6 appears to have only visually improved over time, and that is most evident in the level of detail on protagonists Jason and Lucia. In 2023, we got our first official look at GTA 6 with the first trailer. There had been some leaks prior to this, but this was the first time Rockstar showed the game itself. The game looked stunning with gorgeous lighting effects, vivid colors, and realistic-looking characters. Rockstar would then go dark for a year and a half before re-revealing the game, and the graphical leap was absurdly impressive.

Compared to the 2023 trailer, GTA 6's visuals have drastically changed. The overall art direction remained the same, but the level of detail presented in the character models changed massively during this period. In the first trailer, Lucia's skin looks less textured, more flat, and less nuanced. Her hair also doesn't move much; there's a bit of bounce to her ponytail, but it's more limited. She also has the same hairstyle throughout the entire trailer, outside of some loose strands of hair on the sides of her face in the opening shots.

Jason only gets a few seconds to shine, but he largely looks like a generic white guy with his shaved head and stubble. Trailer 2, however, provides a lot more depth. Both characters sport a variety of hairstyles, with Lucia rocking wavy hair and a golden dress. Jason's brown hair flows out of the back of his hat. His skin glistens after sweating in the Vice City heat, his veins outline his arms, and his facial hair appears to be somewhat uneven, with certain strands of hair poking out slightly further than others. These human imperfections are perfections in the world of a video game trying to emulate realistic people. The light also bounces off of their skin in a more natural way.

It's a clear showcase of not only the level of detail, but also the amount of customization the player will have. That mindset carried into the recent extended look for GTA 6. The visual leap wasn't as large as the one between trailer 1 and 2, but it does feel like a world of difference from trailer 1 itself. There's infinitely more customization options and Jason and Lucia are clearly at their final level of polish.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recently stated that trailer 1 was a "mission statement" for the team, as the game wasn't "fully formed." It was a north star for the team to follow and something they could point to as a way of understanding the overall vision for the game. As a result, it makes sense that the game has only improved since then.

GTA 6 is just weeks away from release now and the finishing touches are being added to the game. The ESRB officially rated the game M for Mature this morning and Rockstar is starting to ramp up its marketing efforts with physical ads in places like Miami and New York. After years of waiting, GTA 6 will finally be here on November 19.

items.title: Ahead of Metro 2039, Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light Are Getting Next-Gen Updates
items.description: Metro 2039 is not too far away, launching on February 4, 2027. While that game will truly bring the franchise into the current generation, developer 4A Games is launching next-gen updates for the first two games.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Metro 2039 is not terribly far away now, launching on February 4, 2027. While that game will truly bring the franchise to current generation consoles, developer 4A Games is launching next-gen updates for the first two games.

Both Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light were incredible tech showcases for their time, but they haven't exactly aged gracefully. Despite getting an intial remaster all the way back in 2014, Metro 2033 doesn't play super well with modern hardware, and I've needed to tweak it every time I've gone back to play it. Luckily, these next-gen updates should bring some long-needed bug fixes to the game.

The update will look different on console and on PC. For PS5 and Xbox Series X, the Metro games will run at either native 4K at 60 fps or an upscaled 4K at 120 fps, with PSSR on PS5 Pro and traditional temporal upscaling on the Xbox consoles. Over on PC, though, the game will finally have DLSS support, along with some unnamed quality-of-life improvements.

4A Games hasn't shared a lot of details on the updates coming to Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light, but it does promise to share full patch notes ahead of its October 22 release on PC and October 29 release on consoles. Either way, as long as the games are more stable, I'm all in.

As a lifelong PC gamer, all three of the Metro games hold a special place in my heart, for all the torture they've put my graphics cards through in the past. Luckily, if you don't like putting your hardware through the wringer, it doesn't sound like 4A is going to add ray tracing or anything crazy to 2033 or Last Light, so they should be significantly easier to run at high settings than they were when they launched in 2010 and 2013.

We've already gone hands-on with Metro 2039, and it seems like an incredible and brutal post-apocalyptic shooter — just like I'd want out of the franchise. The visuals we've seen so far look incredible too, so I can only imagine that it's going to stay true to its roots of pushing PC hardware to its limits. Although, it is launching in the middle of an ongoing RAM crisis, which is going to limit its already niche appeal a bit when the benchmarks start rolling out. Here's to hoping 4A Games finds a way to make a Metro game scalable at launch for once.

items.title: Sony Finally Brings AI Upscaling to Base PS5
items.description: AI upscaling continues to be a huge part of the modern graphics pipeline, and while PSSR brought this tech to the PS5 Pro, the base PS5 was left without it due to its weaker GPU. That's been remedied, though, with QSSR.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
AI upscaling continues to be a huge part of the modern graphics pipeline, and while PSSR brought this tech to the PS5 Pro, the base PS5 was left without it due to its weaker GPU. That's been remedied with QSSR.

In a blog post, Sony detailed a new upscaling model that runs on its base console called Quick Spectral Super Resolution, or QSSR. Just like the PSSR that debuted earlier this year on the PS5 Pro, QSSR was born from the Project Amethyst collaboration with AMD that kicked off last year.

The new model is much more lightweight than PSSR, and so it won't be quite as good at maintaining detail as PSSR is on the PS5 Pro, but it should be much more accurate than the temporal upscaling traditionally used on the console.

QSSR debuts in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei, and the respective developers seem pretty enthused about working the technology into their games. Sony's blog quotes Insomniac Head of Technology Mike Fitzgerald, who said, "QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan’s epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel’s Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5."

Likewise, Jasmin Patry, the Lead Rendering Engineer at Sucker Punch, said: “At Sucker Punch, we’re excited to bring QSSR to Ghost of Yōtei players so that they can experience the world we’ve created with even more clarity and detail. QSSR excels at resolving the fine details in our characters and environments and does so with a level of temporal stability that hasn’t been possible on the PS5 console until now. We’ve long wished that all PS5 players could experience the incredible image quality that PSSR brings to PS5 Pro, and QSSR is a positive step towards that goal!”

The blog also shared a couple of clips from the respective games showing QSSR in action, compared to the standard temporal upscaling on the base PS5, and the results are promising. In Wolverine, the clip zooms in on distant buildings, and while the QSSR sample is still quite blurry – it is a watered down model, after all – it is able to maintain a lot more detail in fine objects than the standard clip on the left.

Then, in Ghost of Yotei, the camera zooms in on foliage in the foreground. In the original PS5 sample, the grass is almost a collection of floating green lines, with aliasing that cuts it up into sections. With QSSR enabled, the grass maintains its actual shape, even if it's still a bit noisy.

Obviously, the model running on the more powerful PS5 Pro is going to be better at maintaining image quality than QSSR ever will. But, the PS5 Pro will now set you back $900, and so this lighter model at least brings this upscaling to more people. Sony does say that it is making QSSR available to all developers, so I'd only expect more studios to use it going forward.

Still, we've only seen this model in action in a couple of clips on Sony's blog, so I'm not sure exactly how well it'll perform. Luckily, the patch for Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will be going live later today, so I'll be able to see how well it holds up. But I do hope it works well, because QSSR could help bridge the gap for anyone who won't be able to afford a likely expensive PlayStation 6 for at least an extra few months.

In a blog post, Sony detailed a new upscaling model that runs on its base console called Quick Spectral Super Resolution, or QSSR. Just like the PSSR that debuted earlier this year on the PS5 Pro, QSSR was born from the Project Amethyst collaboration with AMD that kicked off last year.

The new model is much more lightweight than PSSR, and so it won't be quite as good at maintaining detail as PSSR is on the PS5 Pro, but it should be much more accurate than the temporal upscaling traditionally used on the console.

QSSR debuts in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei, and the respective developers seem pretty enthused about working the technology into their games. Sony's blog quotes Insomniac Head of Technology Mike Fitzgerald, who said, "QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan’s epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel’s Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5."

Likewise, Jasmin Patry, the Lead Rendering Engineer at Sucker Punch, said: “At Sucker Punch, we’re excited to bring QSSR to Ghost of Yōtei players so that they can experience the world we’ve created with even more clarity and detail. QSSR excels at resolving the fine details in our characters and environments and does so with a level of temporal stability that hasn’t been possible on the PS5 console until now. We’ve long wished that all PS5 players could experience the incredible image quality that PSSR brings to PS5 Pro, and QSSR is a positive step towards that goal!”

The blog also shared a couple of clips from the respective games showing QSSR in action, compared to the standard temporal upscaling on the base PS5, and the results are promising. In Wolverine, the clip zooms in on distant buildings, and while the QSSR sample is still quite blurry – it is a watered down model, after all – it is able to maintain a lot more detail in fine objects than the standard clip on the left.

Then, in Ghost of Yotei, the camera zooms in on foliage in the foreground. In the original PS5 sample, the grass is almost a collection of floating green lines, with aliasing that cuts it up into sections. With QSSR enabled, the grass maintains its actual shape, even if it's still a bit noisy.

Obviously, the model running on the more powerful PS5 Pro is going to be better at maintaining image quality than QSSR ever will. But, the PS5 Pro will now set you back $900, and so this lighter model at least brings this upscaling to more people. Sony does say that it is making QSSR available to all developers, so I'd only expect more studios to use it going forward.

Still, we've only seen this model in action in a couple of clips on Sony's blog, so I'm not sure exactly how well it'll perform. Luckily, the patch for Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will be going live later today, so I'll be able to see how well it holds up. But I do hope it works well, because QSSR could help bridge the gap for anyone who won't be able to afford a likely expensive PlayStation 6 for at least an extra few months.

items.title: 'These Jobs Are Not Easy': Ex-Star Wars Boss Kathleen Kennedy Admits 'Relief' After Leaving Lucasfilm, Following Turbulent 14-Year Tenure
items.description: Lucasfilm veteran Kathleen Kennedy has admitted she feels "a bit of relief" after stepping down from her role as the boss of Star Wars, following a long and often tumultuous run.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Lucasfilm veteran Kathleen Kennedy has admitted she feels "a bit of relief" after stepping down from her role as the boss of Star Wars, following a long and often tumultuous run.

Kennedy took Lucasfilm's helm in 2002 directly from Star Wars creator George Lucas, and oversaw the studio as it was sold to Disney, produced a new trilogy of mainline movies, and expanded its storytelling via an array of series on Disney+.

Some of these projects have been hugely successful, such as early seasons of The Mandalorian and the critically-acclaimed Andor. And while the Star Wars sequel movies ended in a firestorm of fan backlash and disappointment, they still raked in billions of dollars.

At the same time, numerous Star Wars projects have flopped hard — or simply failed to get off the ground. Solo was a commercial disaster and also messy behind the scenes, as acclaimed directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller (The Lego Movie, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse) were ditched mid-way through filming. Gareth Edwards was reportedly replaced for Rogue One: A Star Wars Story reshoots, while Colin Trevorrow was replaced during the development of Episode 9.

And then there is the long, long list of Star Wars projects discussed by Kennedy and others at Lucasfilm that have simply been lost to the sands of Tatooine. Most famously this includes The Hunt for Ben Solo and that trilogy of films from Game of Thrones showrunners D.B. Weiss and David Benioff, another trilogy from The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson, and a Knights of the Old Republic idea that could have kickstarted yet another trilogy. Marvel boss Kevin Feige was said to be working on a Star Wars project at some point, as was Luke Cage writer Matt Owens, as was legendary director David Fincher, as was British comedian Simon Farnaby.

A slew of other projects left over from Kennedy's tenure technically remain on the docket, though it is increasingly unclear if any will survive, particularly as Dark Phoenix director Simon Kinberg seems to have been given the opportunity to make Episodes 10 through 12. These include a continuation of Rey's story from director Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, a Dave Filoni story wrapping up the Mandoverse, a Dawn of the Jedi project from James Mangold, a long-gestating idea by Thor: Love and Thunder director Taika Waititi, an even-longer gestating idea for a Rogue Squadron movie from director Patty Jenkins, and a return for Donald Glover as Lando Calrissian.

"I suppose there's a bit of relief," Kennedy admitted of her decision to step down from Lucasfilm, speaking at the Bloomberg Screentime event in Los Angeles this week (via The Hollywood Reporter). "These jobs are not easy and stepping into something like that that George [Lucas] had created was an incredible challenge."

Asked about the challenge of satisfying hardcore Star Wars fans while also appealing to a broad audience, Kennedy suggested this was a "challenge that all franchises [face], certainly something that's been around now for 50 years. You've got people where this means a lot to them," she continued. "But at the same time, the challenge is to try to create something new, something original. So finding that balance is really the toughest thing."

"I mean, I don't think you can do anything in terms of the movie business where every single thing is going to be a perfect hit," Kennedy concluded. "I think you learn things, I always like learning things from the movies that we do, the post-mortems we do on what worked, what didn't. But I'm always proud of the work that's been done."

Star Wars continues next year with ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter and Ahsoka Season 2.

Image credit: Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images for Disney.

items.title: 007 First Light's First DLC Out Now, Adds New Game Plus
items.description: The 007 First Light Extended Operations DLC launches for free today, and adds five different missions to the TacSim mode, along with New Game Plus, new outfits and a photo mode that was somehow missing from the game at launch.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
007 First Light launched earlier this year with the promise of future content being added to the TacSim mode, and IO Interactive has finally followed through.

The 007 First Light Extended Operations DLC launches for free today, and adds five different missions to the TacSim mode, along with New Game Plus, new outfits and a photo mode that was somehow missing from the game at launch.

Four of the new operations will revolve around the Valhalla, the supercar you get to play with in the campaign, like, once. According to the trailer, these Valhalla missions look like driving trials, where you'll use the car's weapons and gadgets to complete challenges on a timer. Unfortunately, you won't be able to just substitute it into other missions where you have to drive decidedly less exciting vehicles – at least not yet.

IO Interactive also added a New Game Plus mode, and that's probably what I'm going to be diving into first, especially with the path tracing update that came out a couple weeks ago. The mode also bring along a new 00 difficulty, which is supposedly significantly harder than the Purist difficulty in the original game. Enemies are going to react faster, some NPCs are swapped for more difficult variants, and combat is going to be way more unforgiving with two-hit kills and a tighter parry window.

Beyond the content additions, though, IO Interactive is also improving weapon animations and enemies will now be able to throw you off of a cliff, just like you were able to do to them in the base game. It's only fair, after all.

This is the first content-based DLC for 007 First Light and is a welcome return for one of the best games of the year so far. IGN's 007 First Light review returned a 9/10. We said: "Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no one has ever managed before, 007 First Light is the best Bond game I’ve ever played."

While I'm sure some folks were hoping for a story expansion, the Extended Operations is free, and should tide people over before James Bond goes on any more official adventures. Hopefully the game will finally come out on Switch 2 next.
